stem: A hose repeatedly crosses a main aisle during every irrigation event. Which control is strongest?

stimulus.alt: Cultivation work-area hazard scan showing an aisle crossed by a hose among other representative workplace conditions that require hazard recognition and control decisions.
stimulus.caption: Use the work-area evidence to distinguish a stronger hazard-control change from reminders or worker-attention strategies.

choices: Post a warning sign and remind workers to watch for the hose during irrigation.
Reroute, bridge, or secure the hose so the repeated aisle trip hazard is removed or substantially reduced.
Limit the aisle to experienced workers during irrigation because they are more familiar with the hose location.
Schedule irrigation during a quieter period so fewer people are exposed to the hose.
rationale: Because the hose repeatedly creates the same aisle hazard, a stronger control changes the work setup rather than relying mainly on attention, experience, or timing. Rerouting or securing the hose reduces exposure at the source. Signs and scheduling can support safety, but they leave the hazard in place and depend more heavily on worker behavior.
